column16: Reviewers should not use Artificial Intelligence (AI) or AI-assisted technologies to assist in the scientific review of a manuscript as the critical thinking and original assessment needed for peer review is outside of the scope of this technology.
column17: Lancet group peer review page, AI and AI-assisted technologies in peer review section. Verbatim confirmed by direct Chrome fetch on 14 May 2026. The page also bars uploading the manuscript or peer review comments into AI tools as a confidentiality matter. Source URL points to the Lancet group page for consistency across all Lancet sibling journals.

column16: Reviewers must adhere to the journal's stated policy on the use of AI or request permission from the journal prior to using AI technology to facilitate their review
column17: ICMJE Recommendations Section V.B Use of AI by Reviewers. Verbatim confirmed by direct Chrome fetch on 14 May 2026. NEJM editorial policies page explicitly states the journal has adopted ICMJE policies on AI use, so NEJM reviewers inherit this rule. Section V.B also bars uploading manuscripts to AI tools where confidentiality cannot be assured and requires reviewers who use AI to disclose its use to the journal. NEJM's own page surfaces only the author side of ICMJE V; the reviewer side lives at the ICMJE source.
